items.title: Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust sells BTC for second straight week
points: Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust (an exchange-traded fund, or ETF — a pooled investment product that trades like a stock and here holds Bitcoin on investors' behalf) liquidated Bitcoin holdings for two consecutive weeks, reversing earlier accumulation.
Back-to-back weekly sales point to a deliberate strategy rather than one-off rebalancing, and may signal caution on near-term price direction.
Continued institutional selling could weigh on Bitcoin's price momentum if the pattern extends another week.

On-chain data (activity recorded publicly on the Bitcoin blockchain) shows whales (holders of very large amounts of Bitcoin) still active, with some exiting while others remain net buyers at current levels.
The split between institutional selling and retail participation sets up potential volatility in the short to medium term.

items.title: Tokenized stock volume up 288% in July, but one Binance token drove it
points: Tokenized stock trading (blockchain tokens that track the price of real equities) hit $11.3B in July, up 288% month-over-month.
Binance's QQQB token alone accounted for $9.27B (82%), helped by zero maker fees through August 31 and a VIP multiplier counting trades at 3x value.
Excluding QQQB, the sector shrank 30% versus June: xStocks fell from $1.55B to $335M, Ondo posted $792M, Backpack $479M.
The underlying QQQ ETF (tracks the 100 largest non-financial Nasdaq companies) fell 6.6% in July, suggesting volume reflected fee incentives rather than real demand.

items.title: Uniswap v4 fee switch triples protocol revenue, UNI up 12%
points: The July 27 fee activation lifted daily protocol revenue from ~$114K to ~$325K within three days, with proceeds funding UNI token burns (permanently removing tokens from supply) — ~$28M since December.
Robinhood Chain produced over half of 24-hour revenue at $170K, ahead of Ethereum $81K (+82% week-over-week), Base $48K and Arbitrum $16K.
v4 charges traders 5 basis points (0.05%) on top of fees paid to liquidity providers (users who deposit tokens so others can trade), instead of taking a cut of LP earnings as earlier versions did.
Critics warn trade-routing aggregators will avoid pricier pools, pressuring LPs to cut their own fees and effectively absorb the protocol charge.
Governance approved the change with 46.6M votes across seven chains; UNI rose 12% in 24 hours to $4.40 and 16% on the week.

items.title: MetaDAO uses prediction markets to police treasury deals
points: Governance runs on conditional markets where traders forecast whether a proposal raises token value over a 3-day TWAP (time-weighted average price), with the first 24 hours excluded to deter manipulation.

Markets rejected discounted OTC (over-the-counter, privately negotiated) deals from Theia Research and DBA/Variant, forcing Theia to re-propose at a 38% premium before passage; a memecoin launchpad bid was also rejected.
Jito, Flash and Sanctum have adopted the framework, including Jito's fee switch and Flash's vote on sharing revenue with stakers (holders who lock tokens to earn protocol rewards).
Unlike Uniswap, Aave and ENS — where frontend fees accrue to labs entities — instructions baked onchain give token holders binding control over treasury flows.

items.title: Tether's excess reserves halve to $4.1B as Bitcoin and gold slide
points: Excess reserves (assets held above what is needed to back USDT one-for-one) fell 51% from $8.2B to $4.1B in Q2 2026.
Bitcoin and gold each depreciated more than 10%, cutting mark-to-market values (current market prices rather than purchase prices) on $5.8B of Bitcoin and $18.8B of precious metals.
Headline $1.5B net operating profit excludes unrealized asset value changes; including them, losses exceeded $4B, with H1 2026 net financial result at negative $3.2B.
USDT's user base hit a record 650M and the CEO called it a 'great quarter.'

items.title: Prediction markets are Robinhood's most lucrative trades
points: Prediction markets (bets on real-world event outcomes) generate ~$23 per $1,000 traded, versus $2.50 for crypto, $1.47 for options and $0.13 for stocks.
They are now Robinhood's largest transaction revenue source, a roughly 9x spread over crypto that shows unusually high fee tolerance among participants.

items.title: Also noted
points: Coverage of Tempo and a BlackRock money market fund (a fund holding short-term, low-risk debt) was linked without further detail.
